subject: ScalePath renewal — capacity reshuffle & tier schedule
messages:
From: Samira Patel <samira@scalepath.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal timing and our throughput needs

Evelyn — thanks for the heads up on renewal. We ran a Q3 traffic spike and expect our monthly token consumption to increase ~2.8x baseline for the next 12 months. Procurement asked me to get you an initial ask: can we move up one tier and lock a higher monthly commit with predictable burst capacity? We also need a short SLA note on rate limits during promotional windows.

Can you send a draft that shows numbers, overage bands, and what guaranteed burst (if any) looks like? I need something to show the finance team by end of week.

— Samira
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Patel <samira@scalepath.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal timing and our throughput needs

Thanks Samira — helpful context. I copied Ben and Marissa to align pricing and the onboarding ops plan. High level: we can propose a stepped monthly commit that starts 2.5x current commit with an automatic midpoint uplift at month 6 if usage stays up. Burst pockets are available as a monthly buffer (separate metered bucket) and we can include a soft-rate expansion window for promotional spikes (subject to a short warm-up and automated throttling thresholds).

I attached a draft renewal showing three options (Conservative, Stepped, Full Ramp) with estimated monthly fees and overage bands. Ben / Marissa — can you confirm the pricing bands and whether we can include a 30% off first-3-months courtesy credit to smooth the transition?

Attachments: ScalePath_Renewal_Draft_20261107.pdf

Regards,
Evelyn
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-03T11:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal timing and our throughput needs

Looping in quick pricing thoughts — Conservative = +1.5x commit at list price, Stepped = +2.5x commit with 6-month automatic uplift to +3x, Full Ramp = +3.5x commit with optional reserved burst pocket (+20% burst at a blended rate). Overage bands: 10% grace, then billed at committed per-unit rate up to 150%, then a higher overage rate beyond that. SLA addendum: we can guarantee regional latency thresholds and a prioritized scheduling lane for committed capacity; burst is best-effort but we'll include a documented soft-fallback (auto-failover to compatible lower-cost variant) rather than hard guaranteed burst.

I support offering a 30% onboarding credit for first 90 days if legal signs the SLA addendum and the deal closes before 2026-11-15. Worth offering to lock the uptick.

— Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Patel <samira@scalepath.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T09:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal timing and our throughput needs

Samira — quick operational note from the CS side: if you choose the Stepped or Full Ramp options, ops will schedule a short onboarding window (2 business days) for KV cache warm-up and to configure prefix caching and batching rules. Those measures substantially reduce cost per token for steady-state traffic, and they help keep latency during spikes. We’ll also propose a canary route for promotional pushes so we can roll back quickly if latency increases.

I've added an SLA_Addendum_Redwood_v1.docx; it spells out the prioritized scheduling lane, latency SLOs, and the escalation path for capacity incidents. Please review and tell us which option you want us to price as final. If procurement needs Po terms, we can attach a short mutual action plan that lists milestones (PO issued, SFTP for keys, onboarding week).

Best,
Marissa
From: Samira Patel <samira@scalepath.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-07T15:43:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal timing and our throughput needs

Team — thanks, this is exactly what procurement wanted to see. ScalePath will move forward with the Stepped option (start at ~2.5x commit, auto-uplift at month 6 to 3x), and we accept the 30% onboarding credit if we sign by 2026-11-15. A couple of procurement asks before I send the PO: 1) confirm the burst pocket pricing (blended rate number), and 2) add a one-line clause that we get a priority queue for capacity incidents during promotional windows.

I'll have procurement send an initial PO to procurement@redwood.ai by Friday EOD. Can you start a draft DocuSign and mark the SLA addendum as Exhibit A? If you can get that over today we can expedite legal review.

— Samira
